Solution 2 is correct; its final answer is 1350√3.

I verified this independently with coordinates. Put A=(0,0), F=(p,0), D=(p,q), C=(0,q). The ellipse has a=45, and the tangency conditions force q=45√2 and b=q/2, so the foci are F₁=(x₀−q/2, q/2) and F₂=(x₀+q/2, q/2) with x₀=S−q/2, where S=45√6/2. The tangent points are Z=(x₀,0) and Y=(x₀+2S/3, q/2−S/3). Solving the perpendicularity condition gives Q=(x₀+45√2(2−√3), q). Since F₁Y ⊥ ZQ, the area is ½|F₁Y|·|ZQ|, where |F₁Y|²=2700+1350√3 and |ZQ|²=32400−16200√3. Their product is 21870000, so |F₁Y|·|ZQ| = 2700√3, and the area is 1350√3 ≈ 2338.3.

Solution 1 (1012.5) and Solution 3 (225) rely on unjustified assertions and give wrong values.
